title: Guided Lab: Clustering knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Guided Lab: Clustering”?
options: Unsupervised methods find structure without using a provided target label. Scaling and distance geometry matter; evaluate cluster quality and stability instead of assuming labels are objectively correct.
The method proves that every prediction will be correct on all future datasets.
The method removes the need to inspect data quality or define an evaluation strategy.
The method always performs better than a simple baseline, regardless of the task.
questions.answer_key: Unsupervised methods find structure without using a provided target label. Scaling and distance geometry matter; evaluate cluster quality and stability instead of assuming labels are objectively correct.
questions.explanation: The lesson frames the topic this way: Unsupervised methods find structure without using a provided target label. Scaling and distance geometry matter; evaluate cluster quality and stability instead of assuming labels are objectively correct. The other options make unsupported guarantees.

questions.prompt: What is a sound first step when applying “Guided Lab: Clustering” to a new task?
options: Tune against the final test set until the preferred metric increases.
Remove records that produce unexpected outcomes without investigating them.
Assume the default parameters are best for every dataset.
Name the inputs, assumptions, and output for Prepare numerical features; then test it on representative data.
questions.answer_key: Name the inputs, assumptions, and output for Prepare numerical features; then test it on representative data.
questions.explanation: Define the input, output, assumptions, and evidence needed. For Prepare numerical features, a small representative check is more useful than blind tuning.

questions.prompt: What conclusion is appropriately cautious after trying “Guided Lab: Clustering”?
options: A higher training score alone proves generalization to unseen data.
An internal estimator score replaces domain review and operational monitoring.
A successful small example is useful evidence about that example, but generalization, risks, and limitations still need separate checks.
A single successful run proves fairness, robustness, and production readiness.
questions.answer_key: A successful small example is useful evidence about that example, but generalization, risks, and limitations still need separate checks.
questions.explanation: A demonstration only supports conclusions within its scope. Evaluate representative unseen cases and report limitations before production use.
